objective: Validate Face-Fit measurement reliability, observable-behavior rubric reliability, missingness, repeated-session stability, and transfer limitations before any numeric threshold or weight is proposed.

governance.changeControl: Protocol, rubric, metrics, exclusions, and analysis plan must be version-locked before enrollment.

samplingFrame: Multiple supported webcam and microphone classes
Varied lighting, framing, network, and room-noise conditions
Accessibility needs and assistive technology represented where consent and safe measurement permit
sampleDesign.prohibitedPractice: No convenience-sample statistic may be promoted as a population norm.

answerTasks: Standardized baseline reading or calibration task
Repeated prompt family with counterbalanced order
taskDesign.baselinePolicy: Baseline collection method must be locked and separated from behavior outcomes.
taskDesign.sessionPolicy: Repeat sessions on different days or conditions as preregistered; do not silently pool.

video: Record declared resolution, frame rate, camera class, framing, lighting, occlusion, and processing failures.
Retain head and posture availability independently.
audio: Record sample rate, channel count, browser processing declarations where obtainable, microphone class, distance band, room-noise condition, clipping, and missingness.
Do not normalize away device strata without a validated protocol.
time: Preserve monotonic timestamps and explicit invalid intervals.
Never convert missing frames, missing speech, or decoder errors to zero behavior.

consent: Explicit research consent separate from product terms
Separate consent for audio, video, transcript-derived timing, and human rating
minimization: Store only fields required by the locked protocol.
privacy.access: Role-based access with audit logging; raters receive only the minimum media and metadata needed.
privacy.release: No participant media, transcript, identifier, or raw rater row may be committed to the repository.

raterTraining: Use a versioned handbook and standardized examples.
Complete calibration before independent production labels.
Blind raters to automated metrics, treatment arm, identity metadata, and other raters.
annotation.independence: Each assigned answer is rated independently before adjudication.
annotation.adjudication: Keep original independent labels immutable; store adjudicated labels separately with a reason code.
annotation.languageReview: Korean filler and repair judgments require authorized Korean-language raters.

exclusions.rule: Exclusions are applied without viewing desired model outcomes.
exclusions.missingness: Report missingness by metric, axis, device, environment, session, and approved fairness strata; missing values remain missing.

reliability: Select ordinal-appropriate inter-rater statistics before data access.
Report uncertainty intervals and category prevalence effects.
Estimate test-retest stability separately from inter-rater agreement.
constructValidity: Compare automated physical metrics with the locked observable-behavior items only.
Do not validate against personality, emotion, confidence, job fit, hiring, health, gender, or deception labels.
distributions: Report robust distributions by task, session, device, environment, and measurement-availability strata.
Separate technical quality metrics from behavior metrics.
fairness: Audit availability, error, exclusion, and disagreement rates across approved strata.
Escalate accessibility-related measurement failures for human review; never impute a behavior penalty.
sensitivity: Threshold candidates, if later authorized, require preregistered alternatives, uncertainty analysis, and held-out confirmation.
Axis weights require a separately preregistered construct model and out-of-sample validation.
analysisPlan.dataSplit: Participant-level development and held-out partitions must be fixed before candidate modeling.

designPrinciples: Quality gates determine whether a metric is observable, not whether behavior is good.
Gate parameters remain TBD until pilot distributions and device effects are reviewed.
A failed gate yields NOT_SCORABLE or INSUFFICIENT_DATA, never zero.

researchQuestions: Are registered physical metrics repeatable across sessions and supported devices?
Can independent raters apply the observable-behavior rubric reliably?
Which technical conditions cause metric unavailability or disagreement?
Do automated metrics have construct-valid relationships with locked rubric items without protected or prohibited inference?

exclusionCriteria: Protocol deviation defined before outcome review

answerIntervalDefinition: Use the locked interview question boundaries; calibration, silence outside the answer, and system prompts are not behavior intervals.
disagreementHandling: Preserve independent ratings, apply a preregistered disagreement flag, and adjudicate separately without overwriting source labels.
approvalProcess: Research, privacy, accessibility, evidence, and engineering owners must approve their gates independently.
productionPromotionConditions: All decision gates must be met with versioned evidence and an explicit production profile approval; Stage 32 satisfies none.
